note: The workflows of add-job-workflows: each a job run on one page (/workflows/<slug>/) and through the MCP server, by the shared chain runner (packages/runtime/src/chain.mjs). A step input is a literal the workflow fixes (listed as an assumption), {"input": name} for a workflow input, or {"from": [step, "output"]} for an earlier step's answer (steps count from 0), with "columns" to carry only the list columns the next tool takes. A workflow input takes its title, help, and unit from the tool field it names; "advanced" ones sit behind More options. "journey" names the learning guide slug that redirects here. The site build runs every workflow through the core and fails if a step does.

workflows.title: VFR preflight
workflows.summary: From the latest METAR to pressure altitude, density altitude, and the crosswind on your runway.
workflows.job: Check the weather, the altitude your airplane will perform at, and the wind on your runway before you go.

steps.why: Read the weather: wind, temperature, dew point, and altimeter setting.
Field elevation and the METAR's altimeter setting give pressure altitude.
Add the temperature and dew point: the altitude the airplane will perform at.
Split the wind on runway 25. A METAR wind is true and runway numbers are magnetic, so the variation is applied.

workflows.title: VFR cross-country
workflows.summary: From your route and the winds aloft to a nav log, the climb, fuel with reserve, and sunset at the destination.
workflows.job: Plan a cross-country: heading, groundspeed, time, and fuel for every leg, the climb, the reserve, and whether you land before dark.

steps.why: Each leg: the wind correction, magnetic heading from the WMM on your date, groundspeed, time, and fuel.
The climb on the first leg: how long, how far, and how much fuel to reach cruise.
Fuel for the route at your cruise burn plus the climb, against what you carry, with the day VFR reserve of 14 CFR 91.151.
Sunset and the end of civil twilight at the destination on your date.

workflows.title: Convert a coordinate
workflows.summary: Paste a coordinate in any common form and get every other form at once.
workflows.job: Paste a coordinate in any form and get it in every other form, each ready to copy.

steps.why: Read the coordinate, whatever form it is in.
Degrees, minutes, and seconds.
Degrees and decimal minutes, as many GPS units show it.
UTM zone, easting, and northing.
The MGRS grid reference, to 1 m.
The US National Grid reference, as used in emergency response.
The state plane zone the point falls in.
The H3, S2, geohash, and Plus Code cells nearest the size you want.

workflows.title: IFR approach brief
workflows.summary: The weather, the holding speed, the entry, the wind-corrected hold, and the visual descent point.
workflows.job: Brief the hold and the approach: entry, speed limit, wind-corrected headings and timing, and where to start down.

steps.why: Read the weather at the field.
The most you may fly in the hold at 9,000 ft.
Arriving on a 150° heading for a hold with a 300° inbound course, right turns.
The METAR wind is true; holding courses are magnetic.
Headings and timing that keep the hold's shape in that wind.
Where to leave the minimum descent altitude for a 3° path.

workflows.title: Drone mapping day
workflows.summary: From the resolution you need to the height, photo count, batteries, where to swap them, and when the light is good.
workflows.job: Plan a mapping flight from the resolution you need: height, photos, batteries and swap points, line of sight from where you stand, and the light.

steps.why: The height that gives a 2 cm ground sampling distance with this camera.
Check that height against the Part 107 ceiling of 400 ft above ground.
The GSD at that height, along and across the flight line.
75% front and 65% side overlap at 8 m/s set the photo interval and line spacing.
At 8 m/s and 1/1000 s, is blur under half a pixel?
The flight lines over your area, the photo count, and the flying time.
How many batteries, and where each flight ends so the next one picks up there, counting the trip home.
Whether every waypoint stays within sight of where you stand (14 CFR 107.31).
When the sun is high enough for even light and short shadows.

workflows.title: GNSS control to OPUS to state plane
workflows.summary: An OPUS position in ITRF2020 to NAD83(2011), then state plane coordinates, the orthometric height, and the combined factor for ground distances.
workflows.job: Turn a GNSS position into NAD83(2011) state plane coordinates, an orthometric height, and a ground distance.

steps.why: OPUS reports ITRF2020 at the observation epoch; bring the point to NAD83(2011).
Which state plane zone the point is in.
Northing and easting in Colorado Central (0502), in the zone's legal unit.
The ellipsoid height as a height above the geoid (EGM96 here; US work usually uses GEOID18).
Grid scale and elevation factor together: how 1,000 ft on the ground reads on the grid.

workflows.title: Boundary retracement from a deed
workflows.summary: Read the calls out of a deed, plot them and check closure, then rotate the bearings to the basis you found in the field.
workflows.job: Plot a deed, check that it closes, and rotate its bearings to your basis.

inputs.name: text
inputs.example: Beginning at an iron pin at the northeast corner of Lot 7; thence S 00°15'00" E 150.00 feet to an iron pin; thence South 89 degrees 45 minutes West 100.00 feet; thence N 0-15-00 W 150.00 feet; thence N 89°45'00" E 100.00 feet to the point of beginning.

steps.why: Pull the bearings and distances out of the description.
Plot the calls, check how well they close, and find the area.
The record's east line reads S 00°15'00" E; you found it at S 00°17'40" E. Rotate every call by the difference.

workflows.title: Lidar bid
workflows.summary: The size of the site, the flight lines and flight time, the batteries it takes, and the accuracy you can state.
workflows.job: Size a lidar job for a bid: the flight lines, the batteries, and the checkpoints the accuracy class needs.

steps.why: The area and perimeter of the site.
Flight lines 60 m apart at 80 m and 8 m/s: path length and flight time.
The energy in one battery pack.
Flight time per pack at a power draw of 900 W, keeping 20% in reserve.
The accuracy class your checkpoints support, to the ASPRS standard.

workflows.title: Developer: index to area
workflows.summary: Choose an H3 resolution for the cell size you want, index a point, inspect its cell and neighbors, and fill an area.
workflows.job: Pick an H3 resolution for the area you care about, then index a point and fill a polygon.

steps.why: The resolution whose cells are about 0.1 km².
The cell a point falls in at that resolution.
The cell's center, area, and boundary.
The cell and its ring of neighbors.
Every cell whose center falls in a block of downtown Pittsburgh.

workflows.title: Can I fly now?
workflows.summary: The wind at your flying height against your drone’s limit, the light, and your altitude ceiling, from a METAR.
workflows.job: Check the wind at your flying height against your drone, the light, and how high you may go, before you launch.

steps.why: Read the wind and gusts from the nearest METAR.
The METAR wind is measured at 10 m; at your flying height it is stronger. Compare it with your drone’s rating.
Sunrise, sunset, and civil twilight, which 14 CFR 107.29 ties to lighting and night rules.
How high you may fly here: 400 ft above the ground, or higher within 400 ft of a structure.

workflows.title: Plan an inspection
workflows.summary: An orbit around a structure: the path and gimbal angle, the detail each photo resolves, and line of sight from where you stand.
workflows.job: Plan an orbit around a tower or building: the path, the gimbal angle, the detail you will capture, and whether you can see it all.

steps.why: The circle around the structure, with the heading and gimbal pitch at each photo that keeps the target centered.
The detail each photo resolves on the structure, taking the orbit radius as the distance to it (a level view).
Whether the whole orbit stays within sight of where you stand (14 CFR 107.31).
